channel.title: Chain Times
channel.description: Chain Times reports crypto news: bitcoin and ether markets, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: Mantle Bridge or Swap: Which Route Fits the Transfer?
item.description: A bridge moves an asset between Ethereum and Mantle; a swap changes the asset you hold. The better route depends on your destination and total costs.

item.title: How Much Native Gas Does a Cross-Chain Swap Need?
item.description: There is no fixed gas balance for every cross-chain swap: fund the sending chain, check any destination needs, and use the quote to see what the route covers.

item.title: What a Stale Swap Quote Means and How to Refresh It
item.description: A stale swap quote can miss current pool prices; check the new output amount, slippage limit and deadline before approving or resending the trade.

item.title: Why cross-chain messages can take time to settle
item.description: Cross-chain transfers wait because the destination chain needs proof that the source action is settled, plus a verifier and transaction to accept and execute it.

item.title: How to Compare Cross-Chain Swap Quotes Before You Send
item.description: Compare cross-chain swap quotes by the amount that should arrive, all fees, route steps and time; then check the minimum output before you approve.

item.title: Match the crypto network before you send
item.description: Match the coin, network and any required memo to the exchange’s deposit instructions before sending, because a transfer on an unsupported network may not arrive.

item.title: When a Wallet Approval Outlasts a Swap Quote
item.description: A wallet approval gives a contract permission to use tokens; it does not reserve a swap price, so a quote can change or expire before execution on chain.

item.title: What to do when a bridge route changes
item.description: If a bridge route changes after you send, check its status first: a refund may be automatic, delayed, on another chain, or in a different token.

item.title: Network School takes Farcaster, adds rules for posting
item.description: Network School is taking over Farcaster and adding conduct rules tied to posting access, putting the app’s moderation model at the center of its next phase.

item.title: Get the Right Token to Repay Crypto Debt
item.description: To repay crypto debt, match the borrowed asset and network, check the live payoff amount, then source or swap the exact token before confirming in your wallet.

item.title: Bridge collateral to Mantle before minting a stablecoin
item.description: To mint a stablecoin on Mantle, first bridge an asset the lending app accepts, confirm it arrived, then check collateral rules, fees and repayment terms.

item.title: How to Check Whether a Token Pause Blocks a Bridge
item.description: A token pause can stop a bridge deposit or payout even when a route is listed; check the exact token, chain pair and transaction before sending.

item.title: Why Cross-Chain Swaps Can Deliver Less Than the Quote
item.description: A cross-chain swap can pay out below its quote when fees, thin liquidity or price moves affect the route; check the final receive amount and each step.

item.title: What a Cross-Chain Swap Fee Pays For
item.description: A cross-chain swap fee can pay for gas, bridging, liquidity and token swaps. Learn how to read the quote and check how much will reach your wallet.

item.title: How Much Should You Put Into a Test Swap?
item.description: A test swap should clear the route's minimums and fees, while keeping the amount small enough that a failed or delayed transfer would not disrupt your plans.

item.title: How to Compare Cross-Chain Swap Quotes
item.description: Compare cross-chain swap quotes by what arrives, after fees, on the right chain and token. Check the route, minimum output and wait time before signing.

item.title: What a Multi-Hop Cross-Chain Swap Really Costs
item.description: A cross-chain quote can hide pool impact, source-chain gas, destination gas and routing fees. Compare the final amount and each leg before you swap.

item.title: Three checks to make before a crypto bridge
item.description: Before approving a bridge, check the destination chain, the token contract and the amount after fees; those details show what will actually reach your wallet.

item.title: How to check a cross-chain swap after sending it
item.description: After sending a cross-chain swap, check the source transaction, follow its status, then confirm the outgoing transfer and token on the destination chain.

item.title: How to Compare Bridge Swap Quotes Before You Send
item.description: A bridge swap quote is a forecast, not a promise. Compare the destination amount after fees, its minimum output, timing, and route details before you sign.
